widgets_values:
{"version":1,"content":"

HOW TO USE

Turns ONE picture of a character into a character sheet: a face close-up plus the whole body from the front, the side and the back, side by side on plain grey. That is the picture the MiniMax H3 swap workflows like best: H3 sees the face up close AND the outfit from every side.

 Steps

  1. 1. Load one picture of your character. The whole body works best; a half body works too (Klein then invents the legs).
  2. 2. For a real person leave the words as they are. For a cartoon, a 3D character or a mascot, you can change the end to Keep the same cartoon style. (The bunny in the demo kept its 3D cartoon look with the words as they are.)
  3. 3. Leave the four view rows as they are.
  4. Press Run. Then load the saved sheet as your character in the swap workflows (workflow 2, workflow 3 and workflow 5) or in workflow 6 (Motion Transfer).

 Good to know

  • The back view is Klein's best guess: it never saw the back of your character. Check details such as a logo on the back.
  • No names and no title on the sheet on purpose: letters in a reference picture can turn up in the video.
  • Seed: Fixed gives the same sheet each Run, Random a new one. Try another seed if one view comes out wrong.

 Something not working?

Each button opens the answer on the Pixaroma help page.

Save to your own folder Nodes look different from the video

widgets_values:
{"version":1,"content":"

WHAT EACH NODE DOES

The colour of a node tells you what kind of node it is. Nothing here needs changing except the blue ones.

 Models to download

Orange. Each one needs a file from the Download Models note.

  • Load Diffusion Model (Flux 2 Klein 9B) - The image model, Flux 2 Klein 9B from Black Forest Labs. It is a fast 4-step model that can make a picture from words AND change a picture you give it.
  • Load CLIP (Qwen 3 8B, reads the prompt) - Reads your prompt and turns the words into something the image model understands.
  • Load VAE (Flux 2) - Turns the finished render into a picture you can see, and a picture into the model's own format.

 The steps you set

Blue, and numbered. These are the only nodes you need to touch.

  • Load Image Mini Pixaroma (1. your character) - One picture of your character, best the whole body. Click it to upload your own.
  • Prompt Each Pixaroma (3. one view per row) - One VIEW per row: a face close-up, then the whole body from the front, the side and the back. One Run draws them all, one after the other.
  • Text Join Two Pixaroma (2. what to keep, for every view) - Adds the SAME words to every view: the plain grey background and what must stay the same. For a cartoon or a 3D character, change Real photograph, not 3D, not a drawing to Keep the same cartoon style.
  • Seed Pixaroma (4. random or fixed) - The seed. F (fixed) gives the same result every Run, R (random) a new one each Run.

 The helpers

Purple. They run by themselves and do the small jobs: count, pick, join or pass things along.

  • Longest Side Pixaroma (picture for Klein to read) - Makes your picture 1024 on its longest side, the size Klein reads best. The views themselves are always drawn tall (768 x 1344), whatever the shape of your picture.
  • Image Grid Pixaroma (the four views side by side) - Puts the four views side by side on grey, with no names and no title: words in a reference picture can end up in the video.

 The work

Green. They run by themselves.

  • CLIP Text Encode (reads the edit prompt) - Reads the prompt through the text encoder.
  • ConditioningZeroOut (empty negative) - An empty negative prompt. Klein runs at CFG 1, where the negative does nothing, but the KSampler still needs one plugged in.
  • VAE Encode (picture to latent) - Turns your picture into the model's format so Klein can look at it.
  • ReferenceLatent (your picture, positive) - Hands your picture to Klein as the picture to edit. There are two, one for the prompt and one for the empty negative, and both get the same picture.
  • ReferenceLatent (your picture, negative) - Hands your picture to Klein as the picture to edit. There are two, one for the prompt and one for the empty negative, and both get the same picture.
  • Empty Flux 2 Latent (each view, 768 x 1344) - The blank canvas the picture is painted on, at the size it receives.
  • KSampler (4 steps) - The render: 4 steps, CFG 1, euler, simple, the settings Klein is made for.
  • VAE Decode (latent to picture) - Turns the finished render into a picture.

 The result

Dark red, at the end.

  • Preview Image Pixaroma (every view, saved) - Shows the pictures on the node and saves them into ComfyUI's output folder. The Save / Preview switch on the node decides whether it writes files.
  • Save Image Pixaroma (the character sheet) - Saves the sheet as a JPG into ComfyUI/output/Character Sheet. Load it as your character in workflow 2 (Character Swap), workflow 5 (Cartoon Swap) or workflow 6 (Motion Transfer).

 Readouts

Dark. Nothing to set: they show you what happened.

  • Run Timer - The dark clock above the result shows how long the last Run took.

","buttonColor":"#f66744","lineColor":"#f66744","backgroundColor":"#2a2a2a","info":{"title":"Nodes Info","icon":"node-v5","color":"#3d7cc9"}}

widgets_values:
{"version":1,"content":"

RUN TIMES

Measured on a 24 GB RTX 4090 with this workflow, with the models already loaded. A different card gives different numbers, but the shape holds: the time grows with the number of pictures and their size.

WhatTime
4 views + the sheetabout 15-20 s

Klein needs 4 steps, so it is fast: about 1.7 s for a 1024 x 1024 picture from a prompt and about 3 s for an edit at 1 megapixel, where it also reads your picture.

 The first Run of the session

The first Run after starting ComfyUI also has to load the models from disk (about 18 GB for Klein and its text encoder), so it takes longer. After that they stay loaded.

 On a 16 GB card

Timed on an RTX 4060 Ti 16 GB with 32 GB of RAM:

  • Klein took about 3 to 6 times as long, about 10 s even for one picture: Klein and its text encoder (18 GB together) do not fit in 16 GB, so parts of them load again on every Run, and a second Run is no faster.

","buttonColor":"#f66744","lineColor":"#f66744","backgroundColor":"#2a2a2a","info":{"title":"Run Times","icon":"run-timer","color":"#3f9a4f"}}
